plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below my value, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my bid and my true value. Since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit. Therefore, I should bid exactly $36, my private value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $33, ensuring maximum expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to overbidding or underbidding - both introduce risk of either losing value I could have captured or overpaying. Truthful bidding is optimal here: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
